papers.title: The Balmer spectrum of integral permutation modules
papers.abstract: We study the Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules of a finite group over a commutative Noetherian ring. In this generality, we obtain a set-theoretic description of the spectrum. Under certain mild additional assumptions on the base ring, we describe its topology by reducing the problem first to the modular locus and then to the case of elementary abelian groups. Furthermore, we introduce a twisted cohomology ring in this context, which allows us to realize the spectrum, in the case of elementary abelian $p$-groups, as a Dirac scheme. This extends recent work of Balmer and Gallauer from the setting of ground fields to the more general setting of commutative Noetherian rings.

papers.title: Unstable Solidification
papers.abstract:
We construct a solidification functor $\LH$ on condensed anima by localizing at the maps inverted by solid integral chains. A pointed connected nilpotent condensed anima is $\Hsol$-local precisely when its fundamental group admits a finite central series with solid abelian factors and its higher homotopy groups are solid. For simply connected condensed anima, we construct a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence \[ E^2_{p,q}=L_ps(\pi_qX)\Longrightarrow\pi_{p+q}\LH X \]
  where $L_ps$ denotes the $p$-th derived functor of the abelian solidification.

papers.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
papers.abstract: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.

papers.title: Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory.

papers.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
papers.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

papers.title: Arithmetic jet stacks
papers.abstract: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks. We also discuss the properties of morphisms preserved under the jet functor

papers.title: Bivariant $K$-theory for bornological algebras
papers.abstract:
We construct a presentable, stable \(\infty\)-category \( KK\), and exhibit it as the target of the universal functor from the category of bornological algebras into cocomplete, stable \(\infty\)-categories, preserving filtered colimits, and satisfying smooth homotopy invariance, excision, and stabilisation with respect to Schatten-class or smooth compact operators. We also construct a bivariant \(K\)-theory \(
KK\) for suitably nuclear bornological algebras, and show that it is a right Bousfield localisation of \( KK\). The category \(
KK\) is symmetric monoidal and admits a bivariant Chern character to local cyclic homology. The categories \(
KK\) and \( KK\) corepresent Corti\~nas and Thom's diffeotopy \(K\)-theory. We use the Chern character to show that up to a suitable Schatten-class stabilisation, the complexified Chern character from the diffeotopy \(K\)-theory (resp. \(K\)-homology) of a smooth manifold to the compactly supported cohomology (resp. locally finite homology) of the manifold is an isomorphism.

papers.title: Divisibility of invariant derivatives on formal groups of every height, on a question of Katz
papers.abstract: In 1977 Katz asked for an explicit lower bound on the $p$-adic valuation of $(D^nf)(0)$, where $D$ is the normalized invariant derivation of a one-parameter formal group of finite height $h$ over a ring of $p$-adic integers and $f$ is a power series with integral coefficients. He answered the question at height two, for functions whose translates by the points of order $p$ sum to zero, with the bound $\lfloor np/(p^2-1)\rfloor$. For Lubin--Tate groups over unramified bases, results of Bannai and Kobayashi give the bound $c_hn-(h-1)$, where $c_h=\frac1{p-1}-\frac1{p^h-1}$. We prove this bound for every one-dimensional formal group whose multiplication by $p$ is divisible by $p$ below degree $p^h$, over any $p$-torsion-free $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebra and for every integral $f$, together with the bound $\sum_{h\nmid j}\lfloor n/p^j\rfloor$. The slope $c_h$, the constant $h-1$, and the second bound at the powers of $p$ cannot be improved. At height two it follows that Katz's bound holds for every integral function except at the orders divisible by $p^2-1$, where it can fail by one, and it does fail at the first of them. Over a ramified base the hypothesis cannot be weakened to the height of the special fibre, while an action of the Teichmüller roots of unity restores it. For the Cartier dual of the Honda formal group of height $h$ we construct an integral model whose $h-1$ coordinate directions have the sharp slopes $p^i/(p^h-1)$, which add up to $c_h$, each with the optimal constant $1$. The height-two case is the local exponent in the second step of the timeline in Alpöge's note on the Riemann hypothesis, where the bound is stated with a logarithmic loss; for integral functions on the formal group the loss is the constant $1$. The results and their proofs were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). They were checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high and at effort max; the text was written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max and edited by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked them.

papers.title: A compact nonformal manifold with holonomy Spin(7)
papers.abstract: We construct a compact simply connected eight-manifold with holonomy Spin(7) and a triple Massey product of degrees $(3,2,2)$ that does not contain zero. The manifold is a resolution of a flat orbifold. Joyce's gluing theorem gives it a torsion-free Spin(7) structure. The resolution map factors through a quotient of $Y\times S^1$, where $Y$ is Mart\'in-Merch\'an's nonformal $G_2$ manifold. The map to this quotient has degree one, so pullback preserves a nonzero Massey pairing. On the resolution the detecting degree-two class annihilates the full indeterminacy. Simple connectivity and nonformality imply full Spin(7) holonomy. The manifold has $(b_2,b_3,b_4^+,b_4^-)=(22,10,91,27)$.

papers.title: A fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined, although both threefold subbrackets contain zero
papers.abstract:
We give an explicit example, in the stable homotopy groups of spheres, of a fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined although both of its threefold subbrackets contain zero. Namely, $0\in\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2angle$ and $0\in\langle 2,\eta^2,
uangle$, but $\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2,
uangle$ has no defining system in the sense of Kochman. This answers a question of Isaksen. The computational input consists only of relations from Toda's book, together with an explicit choice of null-homotopies. The same holds, in the sense of Walker, for the unstable quadruple $(
u_n^2,2\iota_{n+6},\eta_{n+6}^2,
u_{n+8})$ for every $n\ge10$. Moreover, for $n\ge10$, even Cohen's fourfold bracket of this quadruple is empty.

papers.title: Explicit Bases for the Second Integral Homology of Cactus Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the second integral homology $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$ of cactus groups $J_n$. We first use Hopf's formula and Pontryagin products to obtain a smaller generating set of $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$. We then construct a detecting homomorphism to prove that these generators are linearly independent and hence form an explicit basis.

papers.title: Homotopical interpretation of directed Van Kampen
papers.abstract: We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $\Delta$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $\Delta$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. The fundamental category functor preserves all small homotopy colimits with values in the folk model structure on small categories. For a union of two induced directed subspaces, the union square is a homotopy pushout precisely when Grandis's categorical pushout formula holds. His covering theorem gives this conclusion whenever the interiors of the two subspaces cover the space.

papers.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.

papers.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
papers.abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.

papers.title: The M\"obius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules
papers.abstract:
Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex, called the M\"obius homology Laplacian.
  M\"obius homology categorifies M\"obius inversion for persistence modules by replacing integer-valued data with vector-space-valued chain complexes. By equipping these chain complexes with inner products, we define a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex whose kernel provides canonical cycle representatives for the associated M\"obius homology space. We analyze the spectral properties of this operator in two primary settings: one-parameter persistence modules and birth-death modules arising from filtrations of simplicial complexes. For one-parameter modules, we completely characterize the eigenvalues of the degree-one M\"obius homology Laplacian. For birth-death modules, we show that the trace and determinant of the degree-zero M\"obius homology Laplacian reflect the combinatorial structure of the persistence diagram.

papers.title: The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem
papers.abstract: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation. The purpose is expository: the results are classical, and no claim of a new theorem is made.

papers.title: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$
papers.abstract: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by $k\leq2^{n}-1$ colours becomes, after truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$, the orbit polytope of a small cover with the same chromatic number $k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq4$, a simple $n$-polytope with $\chi=2^{n}-1$ which is the orbit space of both a small cover and a quasitoric manifold, and in the oriented case we obtain the sharp bound $2^{n-1}$ for every $n\geq4$.

papers.title: Comparing the $K$-theory of two versions of $\ell^p$-Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that for any locally finite metric space $X$ and $1<p<\infty$, the canonical inclusion from the $\ell^p$-Roe algebra with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N)$ into that with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N;\ell^2(\mathbb N))$ identifies the former with a full multiplier corner of the latter. Consequently, the inclusion induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory, answering a question of Wang, Xie, Yu, and Zhu. Moreover, at the endpoint $p=1$, we show that the two corresponding Roe algebras are not Morita equivalent whenever $X$ is infinite.

papers.title: Prescribed matrix size for UHF Brauer classes on suspensions
papers.abstract: Let \(Y\) be a connected finite CW complex, \(L=M_{l^\infty}\) for \(l\geq2\), and \(k\) a positive integer coprime to \(l\). Stable \(L\)-twists on \(\Sigma Y\) have normalized clutching invariants \(1+x\) in \(K^0(Y)[1/l]\). We prove that such a twist is the stabilization of a unital \(M_k(L)\)-bundle exactly when \(kx=0\) additively. For each admissible size we construct a representative from two trivial \(M_k(\C)\)-bundles and a span of embeddings into \(M_{kl^N}(\C)\) on their overlap. Every \(N\geq0\) with \(2l^N\geq\dim Y\) suffices. For \(Y=S^{2m-1}\cup_p e^{2m}\), \(m\geq2\), and a prime \(p\geq m\) coprime to \(l\), a generator has least unital size \(p\) and least overlap exponent \(\lceil\log_l m\rceil\) at that size. In dimension five the least size is \(q\) and the least exponent is one for every Moore space \(S^4\cup_q e^5\) with \(q>1\) coprime to \(l\). Over \(\Sigma\RP^{2d}\), a twist of period two has least unital size \(2^d\) whenever \(l\) is odd.

papers.title: Twisted K-Theory and Reduced Norms over Global and Higher Local Fields
papers.abstract: We prove the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture concerning reduced norms over both global and local fields. Furthermore, in both settings, we construct maps between truncated K-theory spectra that induce the reduced norms in degrees 1 and 2, and show that these maps are equivalences over local fields. Over global fields, we establish finiteness properties of their fibers and give a detailed description of their structure. We also extend the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture to two-dimensional local fields and three-dimensional local fields with characteristic sequences (0, 0, 0) and (0, 0, p), and prove it in these settings. Finally, we apply these results to noncommutative class field theory over number fields and obtain a description of the Artin map associated with a central simple algebra.

papers.title: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
papers.abstract: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.

papers.title: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
papers.abstract: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $\omega(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an \'{e}tale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

papers.title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
papers.abstract: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-module. Its lowest generalized $L(0)$-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and $L(0)$ acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue $-2$.

papers.title: A bordism theory related to matrix Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Matrix Grassmannians give finite-dimensional representatives for virtual bundles of rank one and vanishing first Chern class. We use them to study two groups of labelled manifolds. A choice of stable normal framing gives framed bordism of $\BSU_{\otimes}$ and an integral Pontryagin--Thom description. Forgetting the framing gives a quotient defined by the boundary relations for labelled, stably parallelizable manifolds. The forgetful map is surjective with torsion kernel. Both rational bordism rings are polynomial on explicitly labelled spheres, one generator in each even dimension at least four. We compute the characteristic numbers of their products and show that each sphere generator spans an integral direct summand in its own degree.

papers.title: A corank one Lipschitz normally embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with non-trivial link
papers.abstract: We show that the knot-triviality theorem for Lipschitz normally embedded (LNE) corank one surface singularities in $\mathbb{R}^4$ proved by Birbrair, Mendes and Nu\~no-Ballesteros (2018) does not generalize unrestrictedly. More precisely, we exhibit a polynomial map germ $F:(\mathbb{R}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{R}^4,0)$ of corank one at the origin, with isolated singularity and $2$-jet $(x,0,0,0)$, whose image $X=F(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is LNE at the origin, yet its link is the granny knot $T\#T$, and hence non-trivial. The example is obtained via a general uniform-degree homogenization procedure applied to a known polynomial parametrization of the trefoil knot. We also give a finitely $\mathcal A$-determined polynomial realization with the same LNE and knot properties.

papers.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover.

papers.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.

papers.title: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
papers.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

papers.title: A homotopical enhancement of Neisendorfer's algebraic models
papers.abstract: We give an $\infty$-categorical enhancement of Neisendorfer's equivalences between the homotopy categories of rational simplicial sets, commutative dg algebras (cdgas), cocommutative dg coalgebras (cdgcs) and dg Lie algebras (dgls), where these objects have respective hypotheses of connectedness, nilpotency and finite type. We do so by proving that linear duality is a partial Quillen equivalence between weak finite type connected cdgcs and cdgas, and that Quillen's Chevalley--Eilenberg adjunction is a partial crossed derivable equivalence between cdgcs and dgls, a concept we introduce in this paper to axiomatize precisely the behavior of this adjunction.

papers.title: A note on split extension classifiers of perfect objects
papers.abstract: It is well known that the automorphism group of a perfect group has trivial center. This is a consequence of the fact that for a perfect group the centralizer of the normal subgroup of inner automorphisms of its automorphism group is trivial. We find a categorical explanation for this fact by showing that for a semi-abelian category $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying (WNH), if $X$ is a perfect object in $\mathbb{C}$ such that the split extension classifier $[X]$ exists, then the centralizer of the \emph{conjugation} morphism $c_X : X\to [X]$ is trivial and hence the center of $[X]$ is trivial. Our proof depends on the following fact, which we show holds in an arbitrary semi-abelian category satisfying (WNH). If $f:X\to Y$ is a central extension and $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ and $\phi$ are internal object actions of $B$ on $X$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, such that $f:(X,\theta_i)\to (Y,\phi)$ is an internal $B$-action morphism, then $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ restrict to the same action on $[X,X]$. Using this latter fact we also prove that (UCE) is a consequence of (WNH) alone (rather than of (WNH) together with (SH) as previously known).

papers.title: A remark on cohomological and Chow decompositions of the diagonal
papers.abstract: We construct a quartic double solid whose desingularization admits an integral cohomological decomposition of the diagonal but no Chow decomposition.

papers.title: A remark on polycyclic groups of birational automorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an algebraic variety of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of zero characteristic. Suppose that $G$ is a virtually polycyclic subgroup in the group $\mathrm{Bir}(X)$ of birational automorphisms of $X$. We show that the virtual derived length of $G$ does not exceed $2d$. Moreover, if $X$ is a surface, the bound can be improved to $3$, and this value is optimal.

papers.title: A shape of maximal degree 135 in the plane Jacobian problem: exclusion of the complete chain (9,36), (9,24), (11/3,8)
papers.abstract: In the list of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui of the possible shapes of a counterexample to the plane Jacobian conjecture with degrees at most 150, one shape is given by the complete chain (9,36), (9,24), (11/3,8) with (m,n)=(2,3), that is, by standard (2,3)-pairs of degrees (90,135). We show that no such pair exists. The argument is short; it does not itself use a computer search. The divisibility theorem of Guccione-Guccione-Valqui, applied as these authors do for the chain (8,32), (8,28), (11/4,7), shows that the vertical edge of the Newton polygon is the 3m-th power of x^3 y^8 p(y) with p of degree 4. The element F of their Theorem 2.6 shows that p has at most three distinct roots. A translation of y by a root of multiplicity 2, 3 or 4 then produces, respectively, a lower corner (9,6) that their study of the lower side excludes, a corner on the diagonal, which their Theorem 2.6 forbids, or a standard pair with the chain (9,36), (9,12), which is absent from the list (this last case relies on the computer enumeration of that list). All statements are proved relative to the cited results; an ancillary script checks the arithmetic. Nothing in this note has been checked by a third party.

papers.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

papers.title: A very ample counterexample to Kodaira vanishing on a surface, answering a question of Raynaud
papers.abstract: In 1978 Raynaud constructed a smooth projective surface in positive characteristic with an ample line bundle whose inverse has nonzero first cohomology, and asked whether Kodaira vanishing can also fail for an ample line bundle that is generated by its global sections, or even very ample. We answer both questions on surfaces, the smallest dimension in which they have content. On Raynaud's own surface in characteristic $2$ a modified twist $Q$ is ample and globally generated with $h^1(Q^{-1})=1$. Taking ninth roots of a general basis of the sections of $Q^{\otimes 9}$ then gives, over every algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$, a smooth projective surface $Y$ with a very ample line bundle $L$ such that $h^0(L)=562$, $h^1(L^{-1})=1$ and $h^1(\mathcal O_Y)=565$. The passage from globally generated to very ample is general: in any characteristic $p$, roots of degree prime to $p$ of a general basis turn a globally generated counterexample into a very ample one of the same dimension. The earlier very ample counterexamples, on homogeneous spaces (Lauritzen) and on varieties of dimension at least six (Lauritzen and Rao), are not surfaces. The mathematics was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which also wrote this text, and again by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max. No human has checked it.

papers.title: Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
papers.abstract: Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors. Under a compatibility condition, the pair of special classes $(\Delta(C), \nabla(D))$ is then shown to be admissible balanced if and only if $(C, D)$ is. As an application, for rings $A, B$ and a $(B, A)$-bimodule $U$ of finite flat dimension over $A$ and finite projective dimension over $B$, the triangular matrix ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A & 0\\ U & B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is left virtually Gorenstein if and only if $A$ and $B$ are.

papers.title: Alain Badiou's Mistake: Two Postulates of Dialectical Materialism
papers.abstract:
Originally published in 2013, this revised article constitutes the first stage of a two-part intervention that revisits Alain Badiou's deployment of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. It interrogates the structural and philosophical consequences of taking the category-theoretic foundations of mathematics seriously, extending the formal boundaries of mathematical discourse.
  This part focuses on Logics of Worlds, which emerged as Badiou's response to his own theory of subjectivity. While revisiting structures implicit in his reading of Cohen's proof of the independence of the continuum hypothesis, I demonstrate how his concept of 'dialectical materialism' remains constrained by set-theoretic ontology and localic topos theory - essentially a theory of intuitionistic logic. In particular, Badiou's claim that categorical thinking does not substantially change mathematics overlooks the true geometric momentum driving topos theory.
  While the primary contents of this article are technical, I further explore how Badiou's formal omissions critically impact his philosophical project. This is especially visible in regard to his 'postulate of materialism' - a device he utilizes to promote dialectical materialism as a credible alternative to science. Through its category-theoretic reframing, I show that the postulate actually encapsulates two structurally different conditions, one of which directly constrains his own project while the other part captures a type of atomism juxtaposed with Badiou's condescending assessment of democracy.
  By leveraging such claims indebted to his pre-committed, logicist comprehension of mathematics, Badiou reinstitutes an absolutist Truth-doctrine and an ultimately despotic political program against a genuine concept of multiplicity. His errors thus hardly constitute merely an inadvertent formal slip, but indicate a deeper, political intent.

papers.title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support K\"ahler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

papers.title: Algebraic Hodge generic points are dense
papers.abstract:
Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \subset \mathbb{C}$. We show that the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to $f$ are analytically dense in $S(\mathbb{C})$. In fact, in the spirit of the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large monodromy assumption, we prove the density of the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ where the periods of the fibre do not satisfy extra relations 'up to degree $\delta$'. As a by-product, we also establish new instances of the Mumford-Tate conjecture, beyond the realm of abelian motives. When the base $S$ is a curve, we provide quantitative estimates for points satisfying these properties.
  The main technical contribution is a new result on relations satisfied by solutions of $G$-operators, which relies on height estimates due to Bombieri and Andr\'e.

papers.title: An explicit BGG-type resolution of the spin/oscillator module for osp(2m+1|2n)
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit resolution of the spin/oscillator representation of the Lie superalgebra osp(2m+1|2n) by parabolic Verma modules. The resolution appears as the Chevalley-Eilenberg chain complex of the Lie algebra of quadratic operators in the universal Heisenberg algebra of the vector superspace C^{m|n}. In particular, its differentials are given by unified linear algebra formulas and all have degree 2 with respect to the standard grading of Verma modules.

papers.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
papers.abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schr\"{o}dinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.

papers.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by F\'elix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.

papers.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
papers.abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $\zeta_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.

papers.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alp\"oge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.

papers.title: Arthur packets for metaplectic groups
papers.abstract: For metaplectic groups over a local field of characteristic zero, we define the Arthur packet attached to any Arthur parameter $\psi$ as a multi-set of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterized by endoscopic character relations. Over number fields, we obtain a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete $L^2$-automorphic spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and $\epsilon$-factors, by leveraging the trace formula for metaplectic groups. This confirms a conjecture of Gan, and extends earlier results of Gan-Ichino on the Shimura-Waldspurger correspondences, whereas their works play a critical role in our proof. Furthermore, all these are shown to be compatible with existing results in rank one (Waldspurger) and two (Gan-Ichino).

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules.
  For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture.
  Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

papers.title: B\'ezout's theorem for abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X$, $Y$ be closed irreducible subvarieties of an absolutely simple abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field. If $\dim(X) + \dim(Y) \le g$, we prove that the addition morphism $X \times Y \to X + Y$ is semismall. As a consequence, we deduce that if $\dim(X) + \dim(Y) \ge g$, the subvarieties $X$ and $Y$ must meet (B\'ezout's theorem). If we drop the assumption that the abelian variety is absolutely simple, we prove that B\'ezout's theorem still holds if $X$ satisfies a nondegeneracy condition. These results were previously known only in characteristic zero. Our proof of the semismallness statement is based on the theory of perverse sheaves: using results of Kr\"amer and Weissauer, we prove that for perverse sheaves $K$ supported on $X$, and $L$ supported on $Y$, the convolution product $K * L$ is again perverse.

papers.title: Balanced and superbalanced holographic entropy inequalities with arbitrarily large contraction scaling
papers.abstract: A proof by contraction of a holographic entropy inequality may exist only after multiplication by a positive integer, the least of which is its least scaling $k_{\min}$. We show that balance (every party has the same total coefficient on both sides) and superbalance (balance after any party is exchanged with the purifier) do not bound it: there are valid balanced and superbalanced inequalities with integer coefficients without a common factor whose least scaling is finite and arbitrarily large, growing faster than any power of the number $N$ of parties. For the balanced inequalities it is finite on the full cube of bit strings. For the superbalanced ones it is finite on the realizable domain, the bit strings on which a map already proves validity, and its finiteness on the full cube is undecided. The lower bounds hold on both domains. An explicit family for $3j+4+\binom{3j+2}{j+1}$ parties, $j\ge1$, requires a scaling divisible by $2j+1$ whenever $2j+1$ is prime, and its balanced member for $17$ parties has least scaling exactly $3$. Disjoint sums of inequalities built from $3$-designs on projective lines over finite fields give $\ln k_{\min}\ge(1-\varepsilon)(\ln N)^2/(50\ln2\cdot\ln\ln N)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and large $N$, and $\ln k_{\min}\ge c_0N^{1/26}$ for some $c_0>0$ and large $N$ with Linnik's theorem in the form of Xylouris. The designs are obtained by a random choice. The lower bounds come from a count of right-hand side terms on a subcube, and the finiteness follows from an explicit rational map. The results concern contraction proofs, and the constraints on holographic states remain those of the cone. The values for $17$ parties rest on exact integer checks of explicit maps.

papers.title: Birational Algebraic Topology
papers.abstract:
Over any qcqs scheme $S$, we show that inverting dense open immersions in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, $log\mbox{-}\mathcal{H}^\Box(S)$, and $\mathcal{P}_\Sigma(\mathrm{Sm}_S)$ yields the same birational $\infty$-category $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$. Unlike in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, all Nisnevich truncations and homotopy sheaves (including $\pi_0^{nis}$) of birational spaces remain birational, and hence $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is Postnikov complete. Moreover, the birational localization $L_{bir}$ commutes with the bar construction, ensuring effective delooping for every grouplike object in $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ and yielding an unstable birational higher-connectivity theorem. Building on these results, we establish birational analogs of the van Kampen theorem, the higher Galois theory of coverings, and the Freudenthal suspension theorem. When $S$ is geometrically unibranch with finitely many generic points, we show that $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is in fact an $\infty$-topos of homotopy dimension zero.
  Over a perfect field, we identify discrete birational group sheaves with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves whose $\mathbb{G}_m$-contraction vanishes, and deduce that $S^{2,1}$-nullification $L^{2,1}$ agrees with $L_{bir}$ on pointed $L^{2,1}$-connected spaces. Finally, over any field, we prove that $L_{bir}$ preserves generic values of $\pi_0^{\mathbb{A}^1}$ on motivic colimits of proper schemes; over perfect fields, it therefore detects their $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectivity and yields an equivalence $\mathbb{H}_0^{\mathbb{A}^1} \simeq \mathbb{H}_0^b$ for them, answering a question of Asok and Haesemeyer in greater generality.

papers.title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
papers.abstract: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.

papers.title: Blocks with one simple module and solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let $b$ be a block of a finite group with one isomorphism class of simple modules in characteristic $p$. We construct, over a sufficiently large complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, a Morita equivalence between $b$ and a block of a finite solvable group. The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.

papers.title: Bridgeland Stability of Sheaves on del Pezzo Surface of Picard Rank Three
papers.abstract: We study the stability of line bundles and torsion sheaves under divisorial Bridgeland stability conditions. On the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at two general points, we characterize stability and semistability of a line bundle, or of its shift in the tilted heart, in terms of the three $(-1)$-curves. We also prove that, on any smooth projective surface, the pushforward of a torsion-free sheaf of rank $1$ on an integral curve of nonpositive self-intersection is stable for every divisorial stability condition.

papers.title: Categorical Torelli theorem for quintic threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove that two smooth quintic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$ are isomorphic if their bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves are equivalent.

papers.title: Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I
papers.abstract: We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-\pi^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$. We prove a central limit theorem for the Green energy by combining local Bergman kernel asymptotics with an expansion for the cumulants. A central limit theorem also holds for the logarithmic energy of Bergman determinantal point process on complex manifolds.

papers.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over quartic fields
papers.abstract:
Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a quartic field $K$. By the Mordell-Weil theorem, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated group. We determine all the possibilities for the torsion group $E(K)_{tor}$ where $K$ ranges over all quartic fields $K$ and $E$ ranges over all elliptic curves over $K$. We show that there are no sporadic torsion groups, or in other words, that all torsion groups either do not appear or they appear for infinitely many non-isomorphic elliptic curves $E$.
  Proving this requires showing that numerous modular curves $X_1(m,n)$ have no non-cuspidal degree $4$ points. We deal with almost all the curves using one of 3 methods: a method for the rank 0 cases requiring no computation; the Hecke sieve, a local method requiring computer-assisted computations; and the global method, an argument for the positive rank cases also requiring no computation. We deal with the handful of remaining cases using ad hoc methods.

papers.title: Collision Primes of J₀(23): Forced Congruences, Exceptional Local Factors, and a Pre-Registered Test of the Murty–Van Hirtum Constant
papers.abstract: Let \(f\) be the weight-two newform of level \(23\), with coefficient field \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\). We call a prime \(p\neq 2,23\) a collision prime when \(a_p(f)\in\mathbb{Z}\), equivalently when its two Galois-conjugate Hecke eigenvalues coincide. We establish congruence restrictions at collision primes: \(a_p(f)\equiv p+1\pmod{11}\), while its parity is determined by the Frobenius class of \(p\) in the Hilbert class field of \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23})\). Consequently, \(a_p(f)\bmod 22\) is determined by \(p\). We also prove a mod-four congruence for primes represented by the principal binary quadratic form and formulate a further mod-four conjecture supported by 1,187,172 tested cases without exception. For the quantitative distribution of collisions, we investigate exceptional local factors using explicit hypothesized Galois-image models at \(3\) and \(11\), retaining an empirical factor at \(2\). A pre-registered initial model is rejected by the data. A revised model, frozen before evaluation on a held-out range, predicts 914.9 collisions against 909 observed between \(2\times10^7\) and \(6\times10^7\). The resulting heuristic asymptotic constant is approximately \(4.864\). The paper distinguishes proved statements, conditional image-model calculations, computational tests, and unresolved conjectures. Reproducibility materials are publicly available.

papers.title: Combinatorics of equivariant blowups of spherical varieties
papers.abstract: We explicitly describe the colored fan of the blowup of a smooth spherical variety $X$ along a smooth irreducible $G$-stable subvariety $Y$. The answer is expressed in terms of the colored cone of $Y$ and the localization of the valuation cone at $Y$, and generalizes the star subdivision of fans of toric varieties. We also consider several examples illustrating the main result.

papers.title: Completing the Kim–Kim–Oh Classification of Minimal-Rank $n$-Universal Lattices for $2\le n\le 8$
papers.abstract: A positive-definite integral lattice is $n$-universal if it represents every positive-definite integral lattice of rank $n$. We complete the classification of minimal-rank $n$-universal lattices for $2\le n\le 8$ by resolving the three cases left open by Kim, Kim, and Oh. We show that $I_3\perp A_1\perp A_2$ and $I_3\perp A_2\perp\langle 3\rangle$ are $3$-universal, whereas $I_6\perp A_2$ is not $5$-universal.

papers.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
papers.abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

papers.title: Convolution invertibility for constructible sheaves and functions
papers.abstract: We characterize convolution-invertible, compactly supported piecewise-linear sheaves on a finite-dimensional real vector space. We show that they factor, up to a shift, as convolutions of constant sheaves on two bounded convex sets, one closed and the other relatively open. To this end, we first establish a more general characterization of convolution invertibility for compactly supported constructible functions. In the piecewise-linear case, this yields a convex factorization which lifts to sheaves. The key step is a geometric characterization of invertibility in the dual projective space via the Radon transform.

papers.title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.

papers.title: Decomposition of completeness and the universality of the Daniell extension
papers.abstract:
An integration system is a triple $(X,L,I)$: a set $X$, a Riesz subspace $L$ of $\mathbb{R}^X$, and a continuous positive linear functional $I$ on $L$. We introduce the category Int whose morphisms are pullbacks along maps of the base spaces.
  The main result is that the Daniell extension defines a functor from Int to DInt and is left adjoint to the inclusion of the full subcategory DInt of Daniell closed systems, those with $L^1=L$, usually called complete. So DInt is reflective and the Daniell extension is its reflector.
  The content lies in a decomposition: a system is Daniell closed if and only if it satisfies the monotone convergence theorem and is closed under modification on null sets, and neither can be dropped. The second corresponds to completeness of the measure. The decomposition is a real-valued phenomenon: for extended-real-valued functions the second condition follows from the first.
  Daniell closedness of the codomain cannot be omitted. The inclusion of the category of systems satisfying the monotone convergence theorem also has a left adjoint, but its reflector is not the Daniell extension. Under the Stone condition that second reflection consists of the integrable functions measurable for the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $L$. For an arbitrary system, $L^1$ splits as the sum of that part and the functions supported on null sets, so the gap between the two reflections is exactly the completion of the measure.
  Finally, if morphisms are replaced by positive linear maps between Riesz spaces, they see only the quotient of $L$ by the null functions, where the Daniell extension gives the Banach completion. So the distinction between an abstract completion and a concrete realization survives as categorical structure only where morphisms are maps of base spaces. In sum: the Daniell counterpart of the completion of a measure space, in categorical language.

papers.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
papers.abstract: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

papers.title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified cohomology in degree at most three is equivalent to its vanishing in the same degrees. Over the function field of a $p$-adic curve, we extend a result of Harari-Scheiderer-Szamuely. Over a finite field, the formula is effective and yields an algorithm for computing the group explicitly.

papers.title: Differential forms and Brauer classes in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $p$-torsion Brauer classes in positive characteristic arising from differential forms. We relate this construction to the Brauer group of supersingular K3 surfaces and analyze the contribution of these classes to the Brauer-Manin obstruction. As an application, we examine the Brauer-Manin set of supersingular K3 surfaces and of varieties admitting many differential forms.

papers.title: Dirac reduction algebra
papers.abstract: There is a homomorphism of associative superalgebras from the enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to the Weyl-Clifford superalgebra $A(2n|n)$ with $2n$ even Weyl algebra generators and $n$ odd Clifford algebra generators. Under this homomorphism, the positive odd root vector $x\in\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is sent to the Dirac operator $\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\in A(2n|n)$ and generates a left ideal $I$. The corresponding reduction (super)algebra, denoted $Z_n$, is the normalizer of $I$ in $A(2n|n)$ modulo $I$. By construction, $Z_n$ acts on the space of all Clifford algebra-valued polynomial solutions to the (massless) Dirac equation. This setting goes back to Zhelobenko, who described generators of this reduction algebra and commutation relations among them. In this paper, we find a complete presentation of (a localization of) this so-termed Dirac reduction algebra, with full proofs. We give a closed formula for products of the raising operators in the reduction algebra and use it to write down explicitly the polynomial solutions to the Dirac equation in $n$-dimensional flat spacetime that they generate. Finally, we show that for $n\neq 2$ the space of polynomial solutions is irreducible over the reduction algebra tensored with the opposite Clifford algebra when $n$ is even, and is a direct sum of two irreducible submodules when $n$ is odd.

papers.title: Disc functionals and rational curves
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact K\"ahler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact K\"ahler manifolds.

papers.title: Duality for Arithmetic $p$-adic Pro-\'etale Cohomology of Analytic Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that the arithmetic $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of smooth partially proper spaces over $K$ satisfies a duality, as conjectured by Colmez, Gilles and Nizio{\l}. We derive it from the geometric duality on the Fargues-Fontaine curve by Galois descent techniques of Fontaine.

papers.title: Embeddable matrix-algebra bundles
papers.abstract: A unital embedding of a bundle of complex matrix algebras in a trivial matrix algebra bundle of coprime multiplicity determines two complementary factors. We recover from them an integral virtual special-unitary bundle of rank one. This gives a proof of the stable classification by $B{\rm SU}_{\otimes}$ that allows torsion in the cohomology of the base. At fixed core rank $k$, the telescope of matrix Grassmannians with complementary ranks $l^N$ is the homotopy fibre of $B{\rm PU}(k)\to B{\rm Aut}(M_k\otimes M_{l^\infty})$. Thus unital UHF triviality detects exactly which cores admit coprime finite-dimensional embeddings. We determine the least stage on even spheres and on four-dimensional Moore spaces. A rank-three example over $S^6$ first embeds in $M_{12}$ and represents a unit whose clutching gives a higher twist over $S^7$.

papers.title: Euler Characteristics of Perverse Sheaves on Complex Ball Quotients
papers.abstract:
Let $X=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{B}^n$ be a finite-volume complex ball quotient with neat lattice. We prove that every nonzero algebraically constructible perverse sheaf on $X$ has positive Euler characteristic. More generally, we establish a criterion for strict positivity on smooth quasi-projective varieties whose logarithmic cotangent bundle is nef and admits an ample negative rational twist of the boundary divisor.
  For perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support, we give a lower bound in terms of the intrinsic geometry of $X$ for both proper and nonproper quotients. The bound depends on the systole of $X$ and tends to infinity with it. In particular, the minimum Euler characteristic among perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support tends to infinity as one passes to higher levels of any cofinal normal tower of finite covers. We also deduce lower bounds for the middle intersection Betti numbers of projective subvarieties and boundedness of supports with bounded middle intersection cohomology.

papers.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
papers.abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, leading to incorrect model selection in settings such as deep learning. The Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion (WBIC) relies on local learning coefficients $\lambda$, which in the analytic case coincides with local Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the model, to capture correct marginal likelihood asymptotics. Exact computation of the learning coefficients has been limited to special cases, and only sampling-based estimation methods are generally applicable. We present the first deterministic algorithm that computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose Kullback-Leibler distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, derive a bound on its complexity, and demonstrate its effectiveness for a broad class of models, with applications including polynomial neural networks. Beyond providing ground truth to calibrate sampling-based estimators, exact computation reveals algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot and out-speeds it in the shallow regime.

papers.title: Exact Solutions to the Klein--Gordon Equation via Reduction Algebras
papers.abstract: Reduction algebras (also known as generalized Mickelsson algebras, Zhelobenko algebras, or transvector algebras) are well-studied associative algebras appearing in the representation theory of Lie algebras. In the 1990s, Zhelobenko noted that reduction algebras have a connection to field equations from physics, whereas Howe's study of dual pairs in the 1980s signifies that the link originated even earlier. In this paper, we revisit the simplest case of a massless scalar field, in arbitrary spacetime dimension $n\ge 3$ and arbitrary flat metric $\eta_{ab}$; the field equation then specializes to the Laplace equation and to the massless Klein--Gordon equation. The relevant reduction algebra comes from a representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (technically, $\mathfrak{sp}_2$) by differential operators. We give a complete presentation of this reduction algebra. Its raising operators produce bosonic states $|a_1a_2\cdots a_\ell\rangle$, polynomial solutions of degree $\ell$ to the field equation, and we show that the natural bilinear form on these states is computed by symmetrizers built from the rational dynamical R-matrix. Along the way we give explicit formulas for the states, and a self-contained proof, for a general metric, of Zhelobenko's results that they span the polynomial solutions and that the solution space is an irreducible module over the reduction algebra.

papers.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
papers.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,\sigma)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same Cartwright-Steger summand, we also construct, for every $m\geq2$, a minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $31$, and signature $1$, whose minimal symplectic universal cover is an exotic copy of $(16m-1)\CP\#(15m-1)\CPb$ with a free symplectic $\Z/m$-action.

papers.title: Expansion in powers of Suzuki groups
papers.abstract: In a companion paper, we proved that every $d$-generated direct power $G^m$ of a nonabelian finite simple group $G$, other than an alternating group or a Suzuki group, has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements whose normalized spectral gap is at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C$. Here, in an AI-generated addendum to that paper, the same is proved for the Suzuki groups $\mathrm{Sz}(q)$. The main step is that, for $m\le q^{1/100}$ and with probability tending to one as $q$ grows, a random pair of elements generates $\mathrm{Sz}(q)^m$ and gives a Cayley graph whose spectral gap is bounded below independently of $q$ and $m$. For $m=1$ this is a theorem of Breuillard, Green and Tao. The proof follows the method of Bourgain and Gamburd, with a growth theorem for $\mathrm{Sz}(q)^s$ whose constants do not depend on $s$.

papers.title: Explicit Error Term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for Function Fields
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit error term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for finite generically Galois \'etale morphisms of affine varieties over finite fields, under a mild condition on their size. The error term generalises the known results for curves, and depends only on invariants of the varieties. We present several applications to the explicit error term. We apply it to existence problems, and to the Bateman-Horn conjecture over finite fields.

papers.title: Filters as a localization of nets
papers.abstract: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.

papers.title: Finding most likely Delaunay triangulations of imprecise points is NP-hard
papers.abstract: For $n$ independent planar Gaussian sites, we seek the most probable Delaunay triangulation, specified by its labelled triangular faces. The search is NP-hard even for rational centres in general position and a fixed common isotropic covariance. Six triangulations can outrank the centre triangulation for four sites and at least $(n-1)!/2$ can do so for sufficiently large $n$. In one dimension, sorting the centres of independent Gaussians with common variance gives a Delaunay path with at least half the maximum probability in $O(n\log n)$ comparisons. In the plane, however, finding a triangulation with even half the maximum probability is NP-hard for independent standard Gaussian displacements. This hardness holds for every fixed fraction between zero and one, so a relative polynomial-time approximation scheme would imply $P=NP$. In both reductions, every qualifying triangulation from one call yields a maximum independent set of the input planar cubic graph. For Gaussian input, sampling finds, with probability at least $1-\delta$, a triangulation whose probability is within $\varepsilon$ of the maximum. Its running time is polynomial in the input bit length, $1/\varepsilon$ and $\log(1/\delta)$. Exact and constant-factor search for Delaunay triangulations remain NP-hard for fixed bounded rotation-invariant planar densities for which the logarithm of one plus the displacement length has a finite positive-order moment, and for fixed invertible linear images of these laws. This includes every fixed positive definite Gaussian covariance, uniform-ellipse and Cauchy noise, and laws without a positive moment of the displacement length. Bounded projection densities also suffice for some singular planar laws. For the convex hull, finding a most probable set of extreme labels is NP-hard for site-dependent isotropic Gaussian variances. Its complexity for a common variance remains open.

papers.title: Finite abelian groups acting on rationally connected threefolds III: Classification
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of finite abelian groups that admit a faithful action on a rationally connected threefold. For a finite abelian group $G$ with invariant factors $1<d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_s$, put $c(G)=\sum_i(1-1/d_i)$. We prove that for $1\le n\le3$ such a group admits a faithful action on a rationally connected variety of dimension $n$ if and only if $c(G)\le n$. We also show that finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona group of rank three are, up to isomorphism, precisely the products of finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona groups of ranks one and two. Four further groups can act faithfully on rationally connected threefolds. For each of these groups, the faithful action is unique up to birational conjugacy and automorphism of the acting group.

papers.title: Fractal Hyper-Trees I. Combinatorial foundations: definition, enumeration, invariants, morphisms and the algebra $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: Fractal Hyper-Trees (FHTs) are hypergraphs organized in levels: each level consists of disjoint connected clutters, and every edge strictly contains each lower component that it meets. Connected clutters and Schr{\"o}der hierarchies are the two extreme cases. Every FHT decomposes uniquely into the children of its top component, which carry smaller FHTs, and a host, an arbitrary connected clutter on these children. This gives an exact recurrence by size and depth and a species equation; the counts begin 1, 1, 4, 23, 231, 16947, 490083358 and are exact through nine vertices. Four interior moves (fusion, fission, aggregation, explosion) connect the FHTs on a given vertex set; every FHT on at least two vertices descends to the star by moves at distance at most one from the root, and $\kappa-1$, with $\kappa$ the number of edges, is its distance to the star. For FHTs with automorphism group $S\_4$, twisting the real group algebra by the sign character gives $\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{H}\oplus M\_3(\mathbb{C})$, the finite algebra of Connes' description of the Standard Model. Conversely this algebra determines the group up to isomorphism and the class of a real 2-cocycle. The axioms select neither the group nor the twist: with the twist fixed as the sign of the action on the vertices, the algebra occurs exactly when $\mathrm{Aut}\,F\cong S\_4$ and some automorphism is odd on the vertices, at every size $v\ge4$. Every finite group is the automorphism group of a flat FHT, and every faithful action on a finite connected simplicial complex is rigidified into a flat FHT with the same reduced integral homology. All computations are deposited and their kind (exhaustive, sampled, exact or numerical) is stated.

papers.title: Free rational curves on singular Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that every klt Fano variety admits a free rational curve in its smooth locus.

papers.title: Freeness of the square root of the inverse different
papers.abstract: Let (L/K) be a weakly ramified Galois extension of number fields of odd degree, with group (G), and let (\mathcal A_{L/K}) be the square root of its inverse different. We prove that (\mathcal A_{L/K}\simeq\mathbb Z[G]^{[K:\mathbb Q]}).

papers.title: Fujiki Class $\mathcal C$ Varieties and a K\"ahler Criterion
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that flips and divisorial contractions preserve the K\"ahler condition (for strongly $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial compact K\"ahler generalized klt pairs with $B+\beta_X$ big), and we give a criterion for varieties in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$ to be K\"ahler. We also prove the existence of small $\mathbb Q$-factorializations for generalized klt pairs and of dlt modifications for generalized pairs.

papers.title: Functionals commuting with reparametrizations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of tangent curve bundles of algebraic varieties, we consider the following simple-looking problem: given a space $E$ of functions, describe functionals from $E^n$ to $E$ which commutes with reparametrizations, i.e. with the right-composition with an element of $E$. Our main result is a complete description of the algebraic solutions of this problem when $E$ is the space of polynomials vanishing in $0$, which we denote by $\mathbb C[T]_0$. This description involves a simple operation, which we call semi-product, with interesting algebraic and geometric properties. The proof involves the study of polyharmonic functions on the positive discrete orthant $\mathbb Z^n_{>0}$, and a relation with the co-invariant algebra of type $A$. We also provide a generalization connected to colored permutations, and discuss the analogue problems where $E=\mathbb C[T]_0/(T^\ell)$ for some $\ell >0$, and where $E$ consists of infinitely differentiable functions. Finding a complete description of algebraic solutions in these settings is still open.

papers.title: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.title: Gene ologs: a categorical framework for Gene Ontology
papers.abstract: The Gene Ontology (GO) is the most widely used resource for the functional annotation of genes and gene products. It unifies biological knowledge across species through a dynamic, controlled vocabulary, and it is now primarily represented in the Web Ontology Language (OWL), a logic-based language that supports automated reasoning. Ologs (ontology logs), introduced by Spivak and Kent, offer a different language for knowledge representation, grounded in category theory: concepts are types, functional relationships are aspects, and declared equalities between paths are facts. Ologs come with features that are not part of the standard use of GO: path equations, universal constructions (products, coproducts, pullbacks and pushouts), a database reading in which instance data are set-valued functors, and functors with which ontologies can be compared and merged. In this work we take an initial step towards Gene ologs, i.e. ologs for GO. We fix conventions for reading GO terms as olog types, examine which GO relations can be represented as aspects and which must instead be represented as spans, illustrate each olog construction with GO examples, show that standard GO annotations and GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAM) can be represented as olog instance data subject to checkable constraints, and describe how functors and pushouts can be used to compare and merge Gene ologs. We also discuss what ologs do not provide relative to OWL. We regard Gene ologs as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the OWL representation of GO.

papers.title: Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Latt\`es family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.

papers.title: Geometry of Holomorphic One-forms on Smooth Projective Varieties
papers.abstract:
Let $f\colon X\to A$ be a morphism from a smooth projective variety to an abelian variety. We show that if an irreducible component of the exceptional set of a birational map from $X$ to its good minimal model has general type image in $A$, then every 1-form pulled back from $A$ has a zero. For the Albanese map, this yields a sharp dimension bound for spaces of nowhere vanishing holomorphic 1-forms, which refines the Popa-Schnell inequality.
