  Furthermore, we investigate the structure of the spaces of holomorphic 1-forms with zeros, and show that they are linear for large classes of varieties. Also, we construct a delicate example of a smooth projective subvariety of an abelian variety for which the holomorphic 1-forms with positive-dimensional zero loci do not form a linear subset. Finally, we study algebraic surfaces admitting holomorphic 1-forms that have zeros and do not arise from cohomology jump loci.

papers.title: GIT-thresholds for K-moduli spaces of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this note, we confirm the first wall $c_1(d)$ of K-moduli of hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq n+1$, where $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd}$ if $d$ is even; and $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd-(n+1)}$ if $d$ is odd. Before this wall, the K-moduli is identical to the GIT-moduli for degree $d$ hypersurfaces, so we also call this number the GIT-threshold.

papers.title: Global smoothing of singular Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study the problem of smoothing Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties with isolated Du Bois (equivalently, log canonical) lci singularities. For Fano varieties, we show that any such $Y$ admits a deformation to a Fano variety with only $1$-rational singularities, and if $Y$ has only non-$1$-rational hypersurface singularities, then $Y$ is smoothable. For Calabi-Yau varieties, we show first that any such $Y$ deforms to a Calabi-Yau with only $1$-Du Bois singularities. Moreover, if $Y$ has only non-$1$-Du Bois hypersurface singularities then $Y$ is smoothable. Both smoothing statements extend to lci singularities satisfying suitable local conditions. When we allow a Calabi-Yau to have $1$-liminal singularities, a global condition is needed, which we express in terms of the Hodge-Du Bois numbers of $Y$. These theorems recover and generalize results for threefolds of Friedman, Namikawa, Namikawa-Steenbrink, Gross, and Friedman-Laza. In higher dimensions, our results provide alternative smoothing conditions and also extend the work of Friedman-Laza from the case of rational hypersurface singularities to Du Bois lci singularities.

papers.title: Griffiths-Dwork Reduction For Smooth Hypersurfaces in Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We give an explicit Griffiths-Dwork pole-order reduction algorithm for a smooth hypersurface $Z$ in a Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$. Under two arithmetic conditions on $k,n$, and the degree of $Z$, the residue construction describes the Hodge filtration on the middle cohomology of the complement in terms of the Jacobian ring. We explicitly characterize the required cohomological vanishings. As applications, we compute group representations on the vanishing cohomology of two symmetric hyperplane sections of $\mathrm{Gr}(3,10)$ and deduce maximal Picard rank for their associated Debarre-Voisin fourfolds. We also compute a Picard-Fuchs equation for a pencil of symmetric Gushel-Mukai fivefolds.

papers.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
papers.abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.

papers.title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
papers.abstract:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$.
  (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^\gamma y,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $\gamma\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then:
  - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$;
  - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile;
  - a B\^ocher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously.
  The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincar\'e condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links.
  (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\log\rho$ term, $\rho=|x|$.
  (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $\rho^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.

papers.title: Higher weighted Lucas sums and even q-beta values
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the Lucas numbers and $B_j=\sum_{m\ge1}m^{2j-1}/L_{2m}$. At least one of $B_2,\ldots,B_{10}$ is linearly independent of $1,B_1$ over the rationals. The family contains infinitely many linearly independent values. More generally, at every positive real quadratic unit $q<1$ of norm one, the rational dimension of the even $q$-beta values through weight $A-1$, together with $1$, grows at least on the order of $\sqrt A$.

papers.title: Hilbert measures of non-coregular representations of the circle and orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We give explicit constructions of the Hilbert measure, which transports the integral of an invariant smooth function from a representation to the image of the Hilbert embedding, for certain representations of the circle, orthogonal, and special orthogonal groups that are non-coregular, meaning that the algebra of invariants is not a polynomial algebra. These include all $4$-dimension real circle representations, a family of $6$-dimensional circle representations, and $k$ copies of the defining representations of the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups when $k$ is large enough that the representation is not coregular. For the circle representations, we also construct the Hilbert measure on the singular symplectic quotient at level zero.

papers.title: Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite. Furthermore, we give sufficient conditions under which there are no exceptional characters, providing infinitely many new cases of the Hodge conjecture for Klein varieties. Finally, we describe the set of exceptional characters of Klein varieties for small dimensions.

papers.title: Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.

papers.title: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
papers.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $\Sigma A_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

papers.title: How Many Cycle Lengths Can a Unique Quotient Require?
papers.abstract: Given two permutations \(A\) and \(B\), suppose there is just one finite dynamical system \(X\), up to isomorphism, whose direct product with \(A\) is \(B\). How many different cycle lengths can \(X\) have? For every sufficiently large \(k\) we construct a divisor with \(k\) cycle lengths and a target with exactly \(k+1\). Their unique quotient has asymptotically \(\tfrac12 k^2\log_2\log k\) distinct cycle lengths. Every one of these lengths is absent from the target. The divisor is fixed once \(k\) is chosen. Its cycles have lengths \(M/p\), where \(M\) is the product of the first \(k\) primes and \(p\) runs over those primes. The proof chooses a set containing almost all the first \(k\) primes. Each quotient cycle omits exactly two primes of this set. A congruence fixes the number of states assigned to each missing pair. Smaller primes then distinguish several forced cycle lengths within each pair.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Embeddings in Toric Geometry: Effectivity and Deformation Stability
papers.abstract: We study the deformation behavior of Kobayashi hyperbolic embeddings for complements of divisors in projective toric varieties. In the toric setting, the Zariski closure of an entire curve in a torus complement is a translate of an algebraic subtorus contained in that complement. This translates hyperbolicity questions into combinatorial conditions on lattice-point configurations of Newton polytopes. Building on a theorem of Tiba, which guarantees hyperbolic embedding for a general divisor under suitable facewise lattice conditions, we develop an effective refinement of his argument. We construct an explicit constructible bad locus in the coefficient parameter space, characterized by the presence of translated subtori in the divisor or its complement on a torus stratum, and use its proper Zariski closure as an exceptional locus. This description makes the exceptional set amenable to computation. Using this effectivity, we prove a deformation stability result: along any algebraic one-parameter family of divisors whose initial member avoids the exceptional locus, hyperbolic embedding fails for at most finitely many parameters. Under strengthened lattice-point hypotheses, we further exhibit distinguished one-parameter families for which hyperbolic embedding persists without any exceptional parameters. We also analyze deformations arising from diagonal torus reparametrizations. If the initial divisor lies outside $\mathcal Y$, the inverse image of $\mathcal Y$ under the similarity family is empty on the nondegenerate parameter domain, while the smallest possible degeneracy set of a rational similarity presentation is controlled by a multiplicative rank invariant of the scaling vector. Finally, we illustrate the theory through examples in projective spaces and Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels
papers.abstract: We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged. The specified isogeny is twice an isomorphism and has kernel equal to the full $2$-torsion. Each family gives two real rank-two representations, with projective local monodromies of order $5$ at two punctures and parabolic monodromy at the third. Exactly one of the six projective representations is discrete, with image $\Delta(5,5,\infty)$. Reduction at the two primes above $11$ gives six degree-$12$, genus-two covers parametrizing torsion lines. For the family with a discrete constituent, these Borel covers are the triangular modular curves $X_0(5,5,\infty;\mathfrak q)$; the comparison descends to ordered covers over $K$. The generic arithmetic projective image is $\PGL_2(\F_{11})$; the Galois closure of each Borel cover has constant field $K(\sqrt{-11})$.

papers.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.

papers.title: Integer-valued polynomials over a one-dimensional analytically irreducible local domain form a free module: Elliott's non-flatness conjectures fail
papers.abstract: In 2011 J. Elliott conjectured that the ring $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ of integer-valued polynomials is not flat over $D=\mathbf F_2[[T^2,T^3]]$, nor over $D=\mathbf F_2+T\mathbf F_4[[T]]$, and more generally that some local, Noetherian, one-dimensional, analytically irreducible domain has a non-flat $\operatorname{Int}(D)$. This spring H. Ma, with the reasoning system Rethlas, answered Problem 19 of Cahen, Fontana, Frisch and Glaz negatively, with a local domain whose normalization has two maximal ideals. We prove that Elliott's conjectures fail. If $D$ is a subring of a discrete valuation ring $V$ with finite residue field, and $D$ contains a nonzero ideal of $V$, then $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ is a free $D$-module. Consequently $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ is free for every one-dimensional analytically irreducible Noetherian local domain $D$. By Elliott's own theorems, the canonical maps $\operatorname{Int}(D)^{\otimes n}\to\operatorname{Int}(D^n)$ are then isomorphisms and $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ carries a unique compatible biring structure. For Elliott's two rings we write down the polynomials explicitly. The proof patches two free modules along the conductor square and uses a matrix identity of Whitehead and a theorem of Kaplansky. The proof was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). The corollary for analytically irreducible domains and the explicit examples were written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which also checked the proof; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked the whole note again. No human has checked this note.

papers.title: K-moduli with real coefficients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an algebraic K-stability theory (e.g. special test configuration theory and optimal destabilization theory) for log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs, and construct a proper K-moduli space to parametrize K-polystable log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs with some fixed invariants (e.g. dimension, volume, coefficients). All of these are well-known for log Fano $\mathbb Q$-pairs, and the strategy in this paper is trying to reduce the problems (in many cases) to $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case rather than rebuilding the whole program as in $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case.

papers.title: Kapranov $L_{\infty}[1]$ algebras
papers.abstract:
Given any K\"ahler manifold $X$, Kapranov discovered a nontrivial $L_\infty[1]$ algebra structure on $\Omega^{0,\bullet}_{X}(T^{1,0}X)$. Motivated by this result, we introduce the notion of an $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra, generalizing $L_\infty[1]$ algebras, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is a differential graded commutative algebra with unit. We extend standard notions such as quasi-isomorphism and linearization to this setting and establish a linearization theorem.
  As an application, we prove that any DG Lie algebroid $(\mathcal{L},Q_{\mathcal{L}})$ over a DG manifold $(\mathcal{M},Q)$ induces a distinguished isomorphism class of $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is the DG commutative algebra $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}),Q)$. Their unary bracket is $Q_{\mathcal{L}}$, while their binary bracket is a cocycle representative of the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid. All these isomorphic $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures are $\mathfrak{R}$-linearizable if and only if the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid vanishes. In contrast, the induced $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathbb{K}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$ are necessarily $\mathbb{K}$-linearizable, hence $\mathbb{K}$-homotopy abelian.

papers.title: Kim's universal octonary form over real quadratic orders
papers.abstract: Let \(R\) be a real quadratic order with fundamental totally positive unit \(\varepsilon\). Kim's octonary form is universal over \(R\) if and only if \(R=\Z[\varepsilon]\), or equivalently if the discriminant of \(R\) is \(T^2-4\) for an integer \(T\geq 3\). Building on recent work of Kala, Man, Visser, and Yatsyna, we determine the minimal universality criterion sets for classical and integer-valued lattices over these orders when \(T\) is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Koszulity in the category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie Superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is to establish precisely which blocks in the Category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$ are Koszul. It is known that $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ has three blocks up to equivalence; one generic block and two integral blocks. The generic block is known to be Koszul, and the principle integral block is verifiably not Koszul. In this paper, we prove that the remaining of the three blocks of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul. Consequently every non-principal block of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul, which is the category $\mathcal{O}$ analogue, in the smallest case, of a known result for finite-dimensional modules over semisimple extensions of Takiff superalgebras. This is done by explicitly computing the endomorphism algebra of projective modules in this block and then proving that it is Koszul inductively. Along the way, we compute all $\mathrm{Ext}$ groups between simples in this block. To compute the endomorphism algebra we are aided by a computer algebra tool developed in Mathematica, inspired by a post on Stack Exchange.

papers.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
papers.abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties. As applications, we realize the irreducible polynomial representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n}$ on the relevant homology of the fibers of these maps, establish a geometric $(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n},\mathfrak{gl}_{k|l})$-Howe duality and confirm new cases of a conjecture of Douglass and R\"ohrle on generalized Steinberg varieties.

papers.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
papers.abstract: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.

papers.title: Metric structure in Hecke-induced modules for groups acting on buildings
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a thick locally finite building of type $(W, S)$ and $G$ be a locally compact group acting properly and chamber-transitively on $X$. We give a condition on a Hermitian module $(V_0, \varphi_0)$ of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $\mathbf C_{\mathbf q}[W]$ ensuring that the natural $G$-invariant form defined on the induced $G$-module has the same negative index as $\varphi_0$, where ${\mathbf q}$ is the thickness vector of $X$. It implies that induction of Hecke-modules preserves unitarity. In the affine case, this recovers results by Matsumoto, Barbasch--Moy and Ciubotaru. In general, assuming that $G$ is Weyl-transitive, we obtain new irreducible $G$-representations on Hilbert spaces as well as on infinite-dimensional symmetric spaces of finite rank. Using Hecke-modules of Lorentzian signature, we also derive new obstructions to Kazhdan's property (T), showing that the known sufficient conditions in terms of the thickness are mostly necessary.

papers.title: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
papers.abstract: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of twisted maps to smooth pairs
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of twisted maps to a smooth pair in arbitrary genus, and give geometric explanations for the known comparisons between orbifold and logarithmic Gromov--Witten invariants. We classify the irreducible components of the space of twisted maps to the universal target in terms of tropical data, and show that each is built from torsors under semi-abelian varieties coming from Jacobians of the domain curves. Natural morphisms between these spaces for different rooting parameters measure how each component grows: for rooting parameters sufficiently large and divisible, the growth is monomial, with exponent between $0$ and $\max(0,2g-1)$, and the main component is the only one with exponent $0$. In genus $1$ the virtual class is the fundamental class, which recovers the polynomiality results of Tseng and You. We conclude with geometric examples, beginning with Maulik's original genus $1$ example.

papers.title: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
papers.abstract: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.

papers.title: Neural Learning of Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms: a Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: We combine neural learning and geometric diagnostics to investigate the rank and border rank of the \(3\times3\) matrix-multiplication tensor \(M_3\). Using the Bhattacharya--Mesner product, we derive \textsc{MatMulNet}, a differentiable architecture encoding bilinear maps. Constrained refinement yields a length-\(23\) numerical solution with machine-precision full-tensor residual and bounded decomposition weight. Along the explored length-\(22\) branch, the residual instead decreases as the gauge-invariant weight grows. This contrast supports \(R_{\mathbb R}(M_3)=23\) as a working hypothesis. A Laurent-parametrised extension probes border rank, giving a tentative, protocol-dependent motivation to investigate \(r=19\) and the adjacent \(r=18\) case. For \(M_4\), the same diagnostics distinguish bounded numerical solutions recovered from perturbed known schemes, structured residual plateaus, and weight-growing approximations, revealing the dependence of the search on initialisation. Together, the experiments connect approximation accuracy with decomposition growth and identify concrete targets for exact or certified investigation.

papers.title: Nilpotent quiver varieties with multiplicities and symmetrisable crystals
papers.abstract: We construct analogues of Nakajima's nilpotent quiver varieties for quivers with multiplicities, by developing new stability conditions for framed nilpotent quiver representations with multiplicities and exploiting their interplay with Hecke correspondences. Using these new quiver varieties, we extend Saito's geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals of irreducible highest-weight representations of Kac--Moody algebras from the symmetric to the symmetrisable case.

papers.title: Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.

papers.title: Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon
papers.abstract: Recently, L. Alp\"oge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F. Alderliefste. This note gives an exposition of the proof presented there.

papers.title: On $k$-very ample line bundles on blowups of surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article we study the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow ups of some smooth surfaces. We begin by investigating the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow-ups of smooth surfaces with Picard number $1$, extending the previously known cases of uniform line bundles to arbitrary line bundles, under certain restrictions. We then show that for blowups of smooth surfaces with trivial canonical divisor, $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles implies the $k$-very ampleness of arbitrary line bundles. In view of the above, we study $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles on blow ups of certain $K3$-surfaces $(K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X)$. Finally, we provide a result concerning the $k$ very ampleness of certain uniform line bundles on the general blow up of product of curves $(K_X \not\cong \mathcal{O}_X)$.

papers.title: On a definitition of slice regular algebraic varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a complete correspondence between irreducible slice regular algebraic sets and quasi prime radical right ideals in the ring of quaternionic slice regular polynomials. In particular we make use of the definition of quasi prime ideals to give a characterization of irreducibility of slice regular algebraic sets. More precisely, we show that if $I$ is a radical and quasi prime right ideal, then $\mathbb S_{V_c(I)}$, the symmetrization of $V_c(I)$, is an irreducible slice regular algebraic set, where $V_c(I)$ denotes the set of common zeros with commuting components of polynomials in $I$. Combining this fact with the results of one of our previous papers, we obtain that for $I$ radical, $V_c(I)$ is irreducible if and only if $I$ is quasi prime. We also find a complete characterization of quasi prime radical right ideals, proving that either they are completely prime or the radical of the symmetrization $S(J)$ of a completely prime right ideal $J$.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.

papers.title: On Higher-Order Geometric Refinements of Classical Covariance Asymptotics: An Approach via Intrinsic and Extrinsic Information Geometry
papers.abstract: Classical Fisher-information asymptotics describe the covariance of regular efficient estimators through the local quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood, and thus capture first-order geometry only. In curved models, including mixtures, curved exponential families, latent-variable models, and manifold-constrained parameter spaces, finite-sample behavior can deviate systematically from these predictions. We develop a coordinate-invariant, curvature-aware refinement by viewing a regular parametric family as a Riemannian manifold \((\Theta,g)\) with Fisher--Rao metric, immersed in \(L^2(\mu)\) through the square-root density map. Under suitable regularity and moment assumptions, we derive an \(n^{-2}\) correction to the leading \(n^{-1}I(\theta)^{-1}\) covariance term for score-root, first-order efficient estimators. The correction is governed by a tensor \(P_{ij}\) that decomposes canonically into three parts, an intrinsic Ricci-type contraction of the Fisher--Rao curvature tensor, an extrinsic Gram-type contraction of the second fundamental form, and a Hellinger discrepancy tensor encoding higher-order probabilistic information not determined by immersion geometry alone. The extrinsic term is positive semidefinite, the full correction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, and it vanishes identically for full exponential families. We then extend the picture to singular models, where Fisher information degenerates. Using resolution of singularities under an additive normal crossing assumption, we describe the resolved metric, the role of the real log canonical threshold in learning rates and posterior mean-squared error, and a curvature-based covariance expansion on the resolved space that recovers the regular theory as a special case. This framework also suggests geometric diagnostics of weak identifiability and curvature-aware principles for regularization and optimization.

papers.title: On Some Diophantine Parameters of the Cyclic Torsion Subgroups of Odd Order of Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: For elliptic curves $ E $ over the rational number field $ \Q, $ based on Mazur's classical result, we give in this paper some explicit Diophantine parameters for their cyclic torsion subgroups $ E(\Q)_{\text{tors}} $ of odd order. This work is a continuation of the ones in ([Q1], [QZ1$\sim $2]). Such explicit form of parameters might be useful in calculating torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over higher degree number fields.

papers.title: On the K\"ahler MMP and the transcendental base-point-free theorem
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the minimal model program for big gklt K\"ahler pairs, and in particular we prove Tosatti's transcendental base-point-free conjecture.

papers.title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schr\"odinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Sch\"orkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix structure prohibits a straightforward supersymmetric removal. To circumvent this, we transform the equation to a Schr\"odinger operator with drift terms to simplify the structure of the eigenfunction. We then develop tools to study such operators and conclude that said operator has no second negative eigenvalue.

papers.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
papers.abstract: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.

papers.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
papers.abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the Andr\'e-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

papers.title: Orbital Integrals on Unitary Groups and Zeta Values
papers.abstract: We generalize Yun's interpolation formula for orbital integrals on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in terms of Dedekind zeta functions to stable orbital integrals on unitary groups. Our approach combines Xiao's germ expansion of orbital integrals and the Jacquet-Rallis fundamental lemma.

papers.title: Orbits of submaximal dimension for Sylow $p$-subgroups of finite classical orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup in a classical orthogonal group over a finite field with $q$ elements of characteristic $p$ large enough. The coadjoint orbits of the group $U$ play the key role in the description of irreducible complex characters of $U$. In the paper, we provide a classification of such orbits of pre-maximal dimension. As a corollary, we compute the number of all orbits mentioned above. It turned out that each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q - 1$ with integer non-negative coefficients, which agrees with the Isaacs' conjecture.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
papers.abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

papers.title: Parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields) on a formal principal bundle with parahoric structures. This generalizes the reduction theory due to Hukuhara-Levelt-Turrittin and Babbitt-Varadarajan in the case without parahoric structures [7], and Boalch's result in the case of regular singularity [14]. As applications, we first prove that a formal connection is intrinsically regular if and only if it is a parahoric formal connection, in combination with the works of Bremer-Sage [45] and Chen-Kamgarpour [20], providing various criteria for the regularity of formal connections. We then introduce a notion of relative regularity for formal connections and give criterions. Finally, we demonstrate a parahoric version of Frenkel-Zhu's Borel reduction theorem of formal connections [33].

papers.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
papers.abstract: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.

papers.title: Principal subspaces of affine vertex algebras at admissible levels
papers.abstract: We classify generic principal subspaces of admissible affine vertex algebras for all simple Lie algebras. The nongeneric cases occur precisely at denominator two in types $B,C,F_4$ and at denominator three in type $G_2$. The proof uses geometry of nilpotent orbits combined with positive root null vectors. Surprisingly, null vectors needed for our classification are explicitly known and already studied in the literature. We then study the exceptional principal subspaces at the level of their $C_2$-algebras and arc algebras. For $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ at level $-\frac12$ and $G_2$ at level $-\frac53$, we prove classical freeness and obtain product character formulas. In type $C_n$ at level $-\frac12$, classical freeness fails for $n\ge4$. For $n=3$, we combine the functional model method of Feigin and Stoyanovsky, and a flat degeneration of the explicit realization of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ to prove a product character formula, while classical freeness in this case remains conjectural. The principal subspace of $L_{-5/2}(F_4)$ is also conjecturally classically free.

papers.title: Quartic hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{A}^3$ isomorphic to the affine plane
papers.abstract: In 1975 Abhayankar and Moh have shown that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 all polynomial embeddings of the affine line into the affine plane are equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. For embeddings of the affine plane into $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose image is a hypersurface of degree 3, it is shown in arXiv:1912.02144 that they are also equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. We will consider the case where the image is a quartic hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ and classify all such hypersurfaces up to affine automorphisms.

papers.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
papers.abstract: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{\'e}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.

papers.title: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
papers.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

papers.title: Raynaud and Gruson's flattening techniques in Berkovich geometry
papers.abstract: Raynaud and Gruson introduced a flattening procedure for coherent sheaf in the schemes context that rely on sophisticated techniques of algebra and geometry. These methods were later used by Raynaud, Bosch and L\"utkebohmert in formal geometry, and more recently Ducros has developed analogous tools for Berkovich spaces. However, it should be noted that the expression "flattening by blowing up" is, in this context, a little abusive because the flattening process actually requires a succession of blow up and quasi-\'etale morphisms. The aim of this article is to develop a local flattening technique in Berkovich geometry, in the boundaryless case, which only involves blow up.

papers.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
papers.abstract:
Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$. In particular, if $C$ has abelian and toric ranks zero, then $R$ satisfies these conditions. We also give an algorithm to compute the possibilities for the reduction type of $C_L$ given only $R$ and $n$. The main method involves studying harmonic covers of graphs with a cyclic action.
  As a result, we obtain a characterisation of tame curves with potentially good reduction in terms of their reduction type, and a new proof of a result by Liu-Lorenzini-Raynaud regarding the non-realisability of certain reduction types.

papers.title: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
papers.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

papers.title: Relation (IV) of Nakamura and Schneps holds on the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, with an application to the two elliptic points of the modular curve
papers.abstract: Nakamura and Schneps (2000) defined a subgroup of the profinite Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ by two relations, $(\mathrm{III}')$ and $(\mathrm{IV})$, that hold for Galois elements; they proved that it acts on the profinite mapping class groups of all surfaces, and left open whether it is all of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. We prove that $(\mathrm{IV})$ holds for every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. It follows that every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is the product of a Galois element and an element of the group $\Lambda$ of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, which acts on the whole tower of pure mapping class groups by their formulas. As an application we study a character $\delta$ with values in $\mathbf F_2$, defined on the larger group given by the two- and three-cycle relations alone, which compares at level twelve how an element moves the two elliptic points of the modular curve. We prove that $\delta$ vanishes on the normalized elements of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, so that every character extending it and trivial on Galois elements is trivial on $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. The proofs use the theorem of Boggi and Zalesskii on finite $p$-subgroups of profinite completions, the action of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, and the theorem of Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki on the outer automorphisms of genus-zero configuration groups. Relation $(\mathrm{III}')$ is not touched. The mathematics was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode); it was checked by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, which wrote this text and rewrote several proofs, and by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max as second reader. No human has checked it.

papers.title: Resolution of ladder representations for classical groups
papers.abstract: Atobe has introduced ladder representations of the $p$-adic groups $\mathbf{Sp}(2n)$ and $\mathbf{SO}(2n+1)$, which contain the strongly positive discrete series and M\oe glin's representations attached to irreducible Arthur parameters, and has expressed their characters as alternating sums of costandard modules. We show that all the coefficients of this formula are $\pm1$, with the sign given by the dimension of the orbit of the Langlands parameter, and that these representations have coresolutions of Cousin type by costandard modules, whose Euler characteristic is Atobe's formula.

papers.title: Resurgence of the finite-$N$ Curie--Weiss model: metastability, the spinodal, and Lee--Yang zeros
papers.abstract: We give a resurgent description of the Curie--Weiss (mean-field Ising) model at finite $N$ below the critical temperature in a magnetic field. We argue, modulo the standard identification of lateral thimble integrals with lateral Borel sums, that the partition function is the sum of exactly two sectors, the stable and the metastable phase. Each sector's $1/N$ series is factorially divergent, with its Borel singularity at its own free-energy barrier, and the two Stokes discontinuities cancel. As a result, the median Borel sums of the two series reproduce the exact partition function, which we confirm numerically to a relative error below $10^{-28}$ at $N=150$. Lateral resummation of the metastable series gives the imaginary part of the metastable free energy, with Langer's factor $\tfrac12$ appearing as a half-thimble. At distance $\delta$ below the spinodal field, the metastable singularity approaches the origin as $\tfrac{16}{3}\delta^{3/2}/\sqrt{\Phi_0'''(x_s)}$, where $\Phi_0(x)$ is the mean-field free-energy functional in the up-spin fraction $x$ and $x_s$ is the spinodal point. There we construct the two-point Chester--Friedman--Ursell uniform expansion, in which both lateral sums become $(\Bi\pm\ii\Ai)$ and $(\Bi'\pm\ii\Ai')$ combinations with contour-independent coefficients. Tested against an exact Hubbard--Stratonovich representation of the metastable sector, the sixth-order uniform expansion achieves a relative error below $7\times10^{-20}$ at $N=3200$ across the tested values $\zeta_{\mathrm{lin}}\in\{0.5,1,2,3,5\}$ of the linearized Airy variable. On the imaginary-field axis, an anti-Stokes line, the resummed two-phase transseries reproduces the exact Lee--Yang zeros at $N=40$, with absolute errors below $2.5\times10^{-18}$ for the zero nearest the real axis and below $3\times10^{-28}$ for the four farthest ones. The zero at fixed filling $s=(k+\tfrac12)\pi/N$ has a divergent $1/N$ expansion. We determine its first two coefficients by integral inversion and in closed form, express the third in terms of the next Laplace coefficient, and compute the series through order $N^{-30}$. Pad\'e poles of its Borel transform numerically approach the complex barrier action $\mathcal{A}$, where $\operatorname{Im}\mathcal{A} = s$ by construction. Its Borel--Pad\'e sum reproduces the exact zeros with absolute errors decreasing from $4\times10^{-9}$ at $N=24$ to $2\times10^{-34}$ at $N=328$; from $N\approx200$ onward, truncation at order $N^{-30}$ is the limiting factor.

papers.title: Schubert cells for the super affine Grassmannian of $GL_{n|m}$
papers.abstract: We study Schubert cells in the affine Grassmannian of the general linear supergroup $GL_{n|m}$, focusing explicitly on the low-dimensional cases $n|m = 1|1$ and $2|1$. We define the affine super Grassmannian as an fpqc sheaf, describe its bounded-lattice filtration by finite-dimensional superschemes, and provide coordinate descriptions, equations, and morphisms for the cells that arise in low dimensions. For $GL_{2|1}$ the cells in the positive and negative chambers split as odd vector bundles over jet schemes of the projective line, and cyclic cells of $GL_{n|m}$ are jet schemes of projective superspaces. In the mixed-sign chamber the transition functions acquire nilpotent corrections in the even coordinate, and all cells except one are non-split. We also introduce decorations, which record the odd directions of the cells on the lattice graph.

papers.title: Seshadri Regions and the Asymptotic Shape of Multigraded Regularity
papers.abstract: We introduce the Seshadri region of a subvariety, a convex region packaging the classical Seshadri constants with respect to every line bundle simultaneously. We develop the theory of Seshadri regions as a measure of positivity along subvarieties and apply it to determine asymptotic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for ideal powers and symmetric powers on smooth projective toric varieties.

papers.title: Short representations and counting with distinct odd unit fractions
papers.abstract: Every rational number $a/b$ in $(0,1)$ with $b$ odd is a sum of $O(1+\log\log b)$ distinct unit fractions with odd denominators. This gives the order of both the maximum and the mean minimum length at each odd denominator. For the representations of $1$ with exactly $k$ terms, we show that the double logarithm of their number has order $k$ along the odd integers. In fact, for each sufficiently large odd $k$, one can fix the first $k-2$ denominators and still obtain at least $\exp(\exp(ck))$ different endings. Each largest denominator in this family is divisible by all of the first $\lfloor\exp(ck)\rfloor$ odd primes. We also obtain doubly exponentially many possible largest denominators, each attained by doubly exponentially many representations of that length.

papers.title: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
papers.abstract: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Cramp\'e in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, together with four other decompositions of $V$ said to be split. We show that on each decomposition, every element of the first two bases acts in a block diagonal, block upper bidiagonal, block lower bidiagonal, or block tridiagonal fashion. We illustrate these actions using a tetrahedron diagram. We also determine how the elements of the third basis act on the six decompositions. To obtain our results about finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-modules, we use the theory of tridiagonal pairs.

papers.title: Spaces of ratios of schemes and \'etale cohomology
papers.abstract: We introduce the arithmetic topologies on the spaces of ratios for log schemes and prove the basic properties of their cohomologies.

papers.title: Springer's 1951 conjecture on inverse coefficients settled: true at every odd order, false at every even order from four on
papers.abstract: Let $g(z)=z+b_1z^{-1}+b_2z^{-2}+\cdots$ be analytic and one-to-one in $|z|>1$, and let $G(w)=w+B_1w^{-1}+B_2w^{-2}+\cdots$ be its inverse near infinity. Fix $n\ge1$, and let $q$ be the least prime divisor of $n+1$. In 1951 Springer conjectured that, among all such $g$, the modulus of the inverse coefficient $B_n$ is largest when $g$ maps $|z|>1$ onto the complement of $q$ straight slits of equal length that issue from the origin at equal angles. At odd orders $n=2m+1$ the conjecture reads $|B_{2m+1}|\le C_m$, where $C_m=(2m)!/(m!\,(m+1)!)$ is a Catalan number, with equality only for the maps $z+e^{i\theta}/z$. This case was known for $m\le 7$ and for odd functions $g$, and further cases through $m=16$ have been reported. We prove this inequality and the equality statement for every $m$ and every $g$. More precisely, $B_{2m+1}$ lies in the closed disk with center $-2^{-m}C_m\, b_1^{m+1}$ and radius $(1-2^{-m})C_m$. The proof follows the inverse function along a Loewner evolution and bounds its coefficients, by induction, by those of the inverses of the slit maps $z+t/z$. For $n=2$ the conjecture is a classical theorem of Schiffer and Golusin. For every even $n\ge 4$ the conjecture is false. When $n+1$ is not divisible by $3$, this failure is due to Chang, Schiffer and Schober (1981) and Kuznetsov (1988). We establish the failure at the remaining orders $n=8,14,20,\ldots$, and we give explicit counterexamples for every even $n\ge4$. For even $n\ge4$ the maximum of $|B_n|$ is, to our knowledge, unknown, but it is at least a positive constant times $2^nn^{-3/2}$, whereas the conjectured bound is only $2/(n+1)$ when $n+1$ is prime. These results are verified in Lean.

papers.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of B\"ohning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

papers.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the left ideal ${\rm cl}(L)$ under the classification of ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ given in [Berest--Chalykh, 2012]. The proof is based on a dual version of the Cannings--Holland correspondence, which describes left ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ in terms of finite-dimensional spaces of algebraic distributions on $X$, and an explicit formula for the Calogero--Moser index given in terms of these distributions. We apply these results to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions on $X$: we call a holonomic function $f$ strongly holonomic if the Calogero--Moser index of ${\rm Ann}_{\mathcal D}(f)$ is positive, and we compute this index in a number of interesting cases.

papers.title: Tannakian Brill-Noether theory of nodal curves
papers.abstract: Using the Tannakian categories arising from convolutions of perverse sheaves on semi-abelian varieties, we can associate to any subvariety of a semi-abelian variety a reductive group together with a representation. We compute these groups and representations for Brill-Noether varieties of all curves whose generalized Jacobian is semi-abelian, in particular for nodal curves. We also obtain new results on the dimension and non-degeneracy of these Brill-Noether varieties.

papers.title: Tensor ideals of abelian type and quantum groups
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of tensor ideals in linear rigid monoidal categories that are kernels of linear monoidal functors to abelian monoidal categories. We develop general methods and apply them to the category of tilting modules over quantum groups as well as to some representation categories of finite groups. In an appendix on Duflo involutions in monoidal categories, we make a connection between Duflo involutions in the affine Weyl group and tensor ideals for quantum groups, and prove some of Lusztig's conjectures for arbitrary Coxeter groups, at equal parameters, without invoking the boundedness hypothesis.

papers.title: Termination of the Kahler MMP with scaling
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove termination of klt flips with scaling for strongly \(\mathbb Q\)-factorial compact Kahler klt pairs $(X,B)$ with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary. In particular, compact Kahler klt pairs with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary have minimal models when \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, and admit Mori fibre space models otherwise.

papers.title: The 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups
papers.abstract: We determine the 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups over S^4.

papers.title: The boundary structure of the maximum likelihood eliminant of $3\times3\times3$ tables
papers.abstract: The maximum likelihood estimate of the no-three-way interaction model for $3\times3\times3$ contingency tables is an algebraic function of the table $n$, and each fitted cell is a root of a polynomial $E(x;n)$ of degree $511$ in $x$, the maximum likelihood degree of the model. We describe the structure of this polynomial at the boundary. Conjecturally, the leading and constant coefficients factor completely into $103$ linear forms in the counts with coefficients $\pm1$: two-way margins, sums over pairs of complementary boxes, a staircase set, boxes with a full side, the total, and differences of two boxes. We explain each exponent as the Euler characteristic of a boundary stratum, satisfying the conservation identity $870=511+359$ between the $60$ vanishing strata, the interior torus, and the $43$ blow-up strata. On the hyperplane of a form, critical points of the likelihood escape along the coefficient vector of the form, either onto a facet, where the count is the maximum likelihood degree of a model with structural zeros, or into the zero-margin locus of a box, where the count is the Euler characteristic of an explicit residual variety. Up to symmetry, under the assumption that escaping branches move along these vectors, these eight types are the only forms with coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ having this property. The valuations force factors of the coefficients, and near each hyperplane the eliminant splits into the eliminant of the surviving roots and a boundary eliminant on the stratum, which share a collision discriminant at their meeting degree. We reduce the boundary system on each of the $325$ boundary hyperplanes (under all table symmetries) to an explicit eliminant: in closed form for the $99$ facets of exponent one, the junction branch of valuation $-2$ on $N=0$, the $81$ difference forms of exponent four (where the boundary system decouples into two univariate quadratics), the $27$ boxes $B_{223}$ of exponent six, and the $81$ box pairs $P_{112},P_{122}$ of exponent seventeen; for the $9$ slabs, to the $29$ critical points of a master function on the flow space of $K_{3,3}$; and for the $27$ margins, to the $169$ critical points of the model with structural zeros. While the $103$ active forms with $\lambda_{111}\neq0$ send escaping roots to $0$ or $\infty$, on the $222$ neutral boundary hyperplanes with $\lambda_{111}=0$ the escaping roots converge to finite nonzero values of $p_{111}$, so that for $n_0$ on such a hyperplane, $E(x;n_0)$ factors in $\Q(n_0)[x]$. Across all $189$ symmetry types of pairs of active boundary forms, the numbers of jointly escaping branches coincide with the end-coefficient exponents of the boundary eliminants and yield a two-regime restriction law for every cofactor $Q_k$, consisting of same-side codimension-two tents and opposite-side interior plateaus. Finally, we conjecture that the eliminant is the residual resultant of the margin conditions on the no-three-way interaction toric variety: for a generic scaling of the model, the eliminant has degree $2{,}457$, and as the scaling tends to the uniform one, $1{,}946$ of its roots escape along the same vectors into the zero-margin loci of the four box types. Some of these statements are proved, some only under stated hypotheses, and the others are conjectures supported by exact, modular, and numerical computation.

papers.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-K\"ahler varieties, III
papers.abstract:
The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-K\"ahler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives.
  The proof involves the geometry of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, whose Kuznetsov component allows to realize double EPW sextics and cubes as moduli spaces of Bridgeland-stable objects, relatively over the parameter space of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds. A key step is that the canonical Chow-K\"unneth decomposition of special Gushel-Mukai fourfolds is multiplicative; we use this to show that generically defined cycles on the third power of a special Gushel-Mukai fourfold inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. Along the way, we also show that the canonical Chow-K\"unneth decomposition of any Gushel-Mukai sixfold is multiplicative.

papers.title: The Geometry of Banach space operator-valued measures with cyclic dilations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the geometric properties of operator-valued measures with cyclic dilations. Under a localization condition on the normal part of the bidual, we establish James-type characterizations of shrinking, bounded completeness, and reflexivity for projection-valued measures. These characterizations apply to spaces admitting no continuous Schauder frame, including $L_1[0,1]$. Using vector measure representations and interpolation, we prove that an operator-valued measure admitting a cyclic dilation has a reflexive cyclic dilation if and only if the underlying space is reflexive. Under the same cyclicity assumption, we also characterize the existence of cyclic dilations on spaces containing no $\ell_1$ and on KB-spaces. The dilation spaces can be chosen to be order-continuous K\"othe function spaces. Without assuming cyclicity, we give a weak compactness criterion and local variation conditions for reflexive dilations; an example on $\ell_2$ shows that reflexivity alone is insufficient. For a separable space containing no $c_0$, a normalized operator-valued measure is induced by a continuous Schauder frame if and only if it admits a cyclic dilation and has $\sigma$-finite operator-norm variation. Finally, for measure quotients whose synthesis maps admit bounded linear right inverses, we construct compatible cyclic $L_p$-dilations and represent the quotient spaces as inductive limits, with applications to ReLU Barron spaces.

papers.title: The index from a super-point
papers.abstract: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, the ideal is the sum of the Jacobian ideals of a single superpotential and of its two supersymmetry variations. For $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, the ideal is similarly the sum of the Jacobian ideals of the components of a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ superfield, which is a singlet of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ flavor symmetry for gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and a triplet for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The associated VOA for the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ theory is given by the Feigin--Feigin--Tipunin $\mathcal{A}(6)$ algebra. The arc space of Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of $\mathcal{A}(6)$ does not reproduce the vacuum character, and therefore $\mathcal{A}(6)$ is not classically free. Supplementing Zhu's $C_2$-algebra by three relations in the first jet ring, the generalized arc space reproduces the Macdonald index of $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ up to, at least, order $q^{51}$.

papers.title: The Integral Chow Ring of Smooth Non-strict Toric Stacks
papers.abstract: We extend the Stanley--Reisner ring to the non-strict stacky fans introduced by Geraschenko and Satriano. We then prove that this ring is isomorphic to the integral Chow ring of the associated toric stack when the underlying fan is smooth. More generally, we show that this ring is isomorphic to the integral Chow ring of the canonical stack over the associated toric stack for an arbitrary non-strict stacky fan. These generalize earlier results on the integral Chow rings of smooth toric varieties and several classes of toric stacks. We also give an explicit description of the pullback homomorphism induced by a morphism of non-strict stacky fans.

papers.title: The lattice of rainbow bases
papers.abstract: Let \(E\) be the labelled union of \(n\) bases of an \(n\)-dimensional vector space over a field. We determine the integer lattice generated by the incidence vectors of its rainbow bases. It consists of the integer vectors with equal colour sums and component sums equal to the common colour sum times the component ranks, and it is saturated. In particular, the all-one vector is an integer combination of these incidence vectors. Over every field, for every sufficiently large integer \(k\), the multiset containing \(k\) copies of each label can be partitioned into \(kn\) rainbow bases.

papers.title: The local lifting conjecture for dihedral groups of order $2p^n$
papers.abstract:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $D_{p^n}$ denote the dihedral group of order $2p^n$. A local $D_{p^n}$-action is a faithful action of $D_{p^n}$ on the formal power series ring $k[[z]]$ by continuous $k$-automorphisms. The strong Oort conjecture of Chinburg, Guralnick and Harbater predicts that every such action lifts to characteristic zero. This is also the dihedral case of the local lifting conjecture of Obus.
  We prove this assertion for $n=2$ and every odd prime $p$. More precisely, given a local $D_{p^2}$-action on $k[[z]]$, we construct an action on $R[[Z]]$ by $R$-automorphisms whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $R$ is the given action, where $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring finite over the Witt ring $W(k)$.
  For arbitrary $n$, let $C_{p^n}$ be the cyclic subgroup of index two in $D_{p^n}$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ be the upper ramification jumps of $k((z))/k((z))^{C_{p^n}}$. We prove that the action lifts if $u_i\equiv-1\pmod{2p}$ for every $i$. When $p=3$, we also prove lifting under the hypotheses $u_i\equiv5\pmod6$ for $2\leq i<n$ and $3\nmid u_n$.

papers.title: The monodromy conjecture for remarkable poles
papers.abstract: We prove the strong monodromy conjecture for the remarkable numbers of a regular function f on a smooth complex variety. We show more generally that the log canonical modification of f computes the remarkable numbers and gives roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of f.

papers.title: The question of Anderson and Ihara on the pro-p Galois action on the projective line minus three points, at every prime satisfying Vandiver's conjecture
papers.abstract: Ihara showed that the kernel of the outer action of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb Q$ on the pro-$p$ fundamental group of the projective line minus three points cuts out a field contained in the maximal pro-$p$ extension of $\mathbb Q(\mu_p)$ unramified outside $p$, and Anderson and Ihara asked whether the two fields are equal. Sharifi proved that they are equal at odd regular primes if the Deligne--Ihara conjecture holds, and Brown proved that conjecture. We prove the equality at every odd prime $p$ for which the plus part of the Iwasawa module of $p$-class groups of the cyclotomic tower is finite. This holds whenever $p$ does not divide the class number of the real cyclotomic field $\mathbb Q(\mu_p)^+$, which is Vandiver's conjecture at $p$; by the computation of Hart, Harvey and Ong the equality therefore holds at every odd prime below $2^{31}$. At an irregular prime the Galois group in question has generators that the regular case does not have. The theorems of Fukaya--Kato and Wake--Wang-Erickson on Sharifi's symbol map show that cup products of cyclotomic units generate the relevant second cohomology at every finite level, and we prove that this forces the images of the new generators to have poles that separate all words. The mathematics and the proofs were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high checked the deduction from Vandiver's conjecture and the present text of Sections 4 to 6 step by step, with the theorems of Fukaya--Kato and Wake--Wang-Erickson read at the places cited; Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max edited the text, wrote its first two sections and refereed Sections 3 to 6. No human has checked it.

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis for L-Functions of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Frobenius Polynomials and Intersection Cohomology
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius polynomials attached to linearly constrained Kloosterman families, taking the rank-$r(n)=2^n-\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, weight-$(n+1)$ sheaf of the author's companion papers as an explicit input. The present contribution is the passage from that sheaf to local characteristic polynomials and the intermediate-extension intersection cohomology on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$. We prove the local reciprocal-root bounds and the degreewise purity of the completed factors; their weights are $n+1+i$ in cohomological degree $i$. Using the imported arithmetic relative-image identification, we construct a reflection pairing and derive the completed functional equation with positive root number. We also give a canonical Frobenius-equivariant splitting of the fibrewise compact-support/parabolic sequence by separation of weights and examine the comparison on open coordinate-zero divisors. The statements do not assume global arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity or a higher-codimension wild-boundary exchange. An explicit source-and-dependency ledger distinguishes results imported from the companion papers from deductions established here.

papers.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].

papers.title: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor.
